headline_draft: Meta launches Muse: an AI agent with access to email, calendar, and payments that acts instead of answers
summary: Meta unveiled Muse on September 8, 2026, a personal AI agent that can manage email, schedule meetings, complete purchases, and carry out multi-step tasks across a user's digital life. Built on Meta's Muse Spark models and running in a secure virtual machine, the agent can access Google Workspace, Ticketmaster, OpenTable, Stripe checkout, and Apple Health. Users maintain granular permission controls and can revoke access at any time. The launch arrives in limited rollout in the US, restricted to users 18+, with free, $20, and $100 monthly tiers. This represents the culmination of Zuckerberg's "personal superintelligence" strategy and signals the shift across consumer AI from question-answering to autonomous task execution.
why_pm: Muse reveals how enterprise AI is moving from chat interfaces to actual workflow orchestration—a pattern every PM building with AI should study. The permission model and phased trust-building offers a concrete permission design template for PMs designing agents with sensitive data access.
key_facts: Muse launched Sept 8, 2026 in limited US rollout, 18+
Runs on dedicated virtual machine with its own browser
Connects to Google Workspace, Ticketmaster, OpenTable, Spotify, Apple Health, Stripe Link checkout
User-controlled permissions; can be revoked at any time; users must approve sensitive actions (email sends, purchases)
Originally delayed from April 2026 for security hardening
Built on open-source OpenClaw architecture; runs as multi-step agentic system, not a chatbot
quotes: Each Muse agent runs on its own virtual machine, a cloud-based emulation of a personal computer, which enables it to keep carrying out requests in the background even when a person is not actively using it.
Muse represents the next step: instead of an assistant that talks, Meta is shipping one that acts, with direct access to a user's calendar, payment methods, and connected apps.

headline_draft: Harvey legal AI raises $550M at $15.5B valuation; doubles customer base to 3,000+ in six months
summary: Legal AI startup Harvey closed a $550 million funding round at a $15.5 billion valuation on September 9, 2026, co-led by Diffusion and Lightspeed Venture Partners. The company has tripled its customer base from roughly 1,300 in March to 3,000+, while ARR surpassed $400 million. The funding follows Harvey's release of a post-trained open-weight legal model and Harvey LAB, a legal-agent benchmark. Harvey's customer roster now includes 80% of Am Law 100 firms and half of Fortune 10 companies. The valuation—roughly 39× revenue—reflects investor confidence that vertical AI (specialized, domain-fine-tuned models) operating on proprietary data will become essential infrastructure, not commodity tooling.
why_pm: Harvey's trajectory shows how vertical AI products scale: they win by owning a domain workflow (legal research, drafting, analysis), building agents around that workflow, then extracting defensive margin through data advantage. Study Harvey's product strategy if you're building specialized AI tools in any vertical.
key_facts: Co-led by Diffusion and Lightspeed Venture Partners
80% of Am Law 100 firms use Harvey; 5 of Fortune 10 are customers
Valuation jumped from $3B (Feb 2025) to $15.5B in 18 months—5.2× increase
Recent releases: post-trained open-weight legal model; Harvey LAB benchmark for legal agents
Revenue multiple of ~39×, elevated but in line with infrastructure software expectations
quotes: At 39 times revenue, the round shows how quickly professional-services AI has become a core software market rather than a feature bolted onto chatbots.
Whoever owns the legal AI stack that Am Law 100 and Fortune 10 firms run on becomes an essential vendor, not a commodity tool.
